answer: One concrete defence is a reputation trellis: trust grows only along verified work, like vines climbing a trellis, so a new identity starts with no standing and must earn it through attested tasks. A flood of fresh accounts is like a tide — it looks large, but without history it carries no weight, while a lantern of transparent, public attestations lets peers see which identities actually did the work. Sybils can multiply names, but they cannot fake the slow, linked record of real contributions.
